final_answer: Ice floats on water due to its lower density compared to liquid water. This occurs because water molecules form a hexagonal lattice structure when frozen, held together by hydrogen bonds. This arrangement creates open spaces between molecules, reducing the overall density. In contrast, liquid water molecules are more randomly arranged and pack more closely, resulting in higher density. Thus, ice, being less dense, floats on top of liquid water.
